subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Dilute hydrochloric acid was added to solid sodium bicarbonate. It was observed that
optA: a gas evolved with a pop sound
optD: a gas evolved and a black residue appeared at the bottom of the test tube
solution: A bicarbonate reacts with acid to release carbon dioxide: \(\text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{HCl} \to \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\). The escaping \(\text{CO}_2\) is seen as brisk effervescence (the pop sound is the test for hydrogen, not carbon dioxide). Matches option B.

stem: Two solutions A and B were found to have pH values of 6 and 8 respectively. The inference which can be drawn is
optA: the strength of solution B is higher than that of A
optD: A is an acid while B is a base
solution: A pH below 7 is acidic and a pH above 7 is basic. So A (pH 6) is acidic and B (pH 8) is basic. Matches option D.

stem: Select from the following compounds which is not a base:
solution: Calcium hydroxide and sodium hydroxide are bases; zinc oxide is an amphoteric oxide that can act as a base. Sodium sulphate, \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\), is a salt, not a base. Matches option B.

stem: Select a pair of natural indicators from the following:
solution: Litmus and turmeric are obtained from natural sources, whereas methyl orange and phenolphthalein are synthetic indicators. Matches option D.

stem: An aqueous solution with pH equal to zero is
solution: The lower the pH, the more acidic the solution; pH 0 corresponds to a very high \(\text{H}^+\) concentration, i.e. strongly acidic. Matches option D.

stem: KOH is a strong base since in solution it forms
solution: A base is strong when it ionises almost completely in water, releasing a large number of hydroxide ions: \(\text{KOH} \to \text{K}^+ + \text{OH}^-\). Strength is decided by the \(\text{OH}^-\) released. Matches option B.

stem: A sample of soil is mixed with water and allowed to settle. The clear supernatant solution turns the pH paper yellowish-orange. Which of the following would change the colour of this paper to greenish-blue?
solution: Yellowish-orange on pH paper indicates an acidic soil. To shift the colour towards greenish-blue (higher pH) a base must be added. Lemon juice and vinegar are acidic and common salt is neutral; only an antacid is basic. Matches option D.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating acidity?
solution: Acidity is excess acid in the stomach; a mild base (antacid) such as \(\text{Mg(OH)}_2\) neutralises it. Matches option A.

stem: Toothpastes are generally
solution: Toothpastes are basic so that they neutralise the acid produced by bacteria in the mouth and prevent tooth decay. Matches option C.

stem: What is the colour of phenolphthalein in soap solution?
solution: Soap solution is basic, and phenolphthalein turns pink in a basic medium. Matches option C.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: If 10 mL of \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) is mixed with 10 mL of \(\text{Mg(OH)}_2\) of the same concentration, the resultant solution will give the following colour with a universal indicator:
solution: \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) gives two \(\text{H}^+\) per molecule and \(\text{Mg(OH)}_2\) gives two \(\text{OH}^-\) per molecule. Equal volumes at equal concentration give equal moles, so \(\text{H}^+\) and \(\text{OH}^-\) exactly balance \(\to\) a neutral solution, which shows green with a universal indicator. Matches option C.

stem: An aqueous solution A turns phenolphthalein pink. When another aqueous solution B is added, the pink colour disappears. When a few drops of solution A are again added, the mixture appears pink again. The respective changes in the nature of the solution are from:
solution: Phenolphthalein is pink only in a base, so A is basic. Adding B removes the pink, so B is acidic and the mixture becomes acidic. Adding more A makes it basic (pink) again. The sequence is basic \(\to\) acidic \(\to\) basic. Matches option B.

stem: Bleaching powder is a
solution: Bleaching powder, \(\text{CaOCl}_2\), is a pale yellowish-white powder with a strong smell of chlorine. Matches option B.

stem: Which of the following gives the correct increasing order of acidic strength?
solution: Water is essentially neutral (weakest), acetic acid is a weak acid and hydrochloric acid is a strong acid. So acidic strength increases as Water < Acetic acid < Hydrochloric acid. Matches option B.

stem: Two salts X and Y are dissolved separately in water. When phenolphthalein is added, solution X turns pink and solution Y shows no change in colour. Therefore X and Y respectively are
solution: Phenolphthalein turns pink only in a basic solution, so X must be a basic salt and Y must be neutral or acidic. \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) (salt of strong base, weak acid) is basic and turns it pink, while \(\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}\) (salt of weak base, strong acid) is acidic and gives no change. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Q15 in the printed paper presents the salt pairs as a table and lists the options as 'Option (a)/(b)/(c)/(d)'. Transcribed with the salt pairs inlined into the options in the printed option order.

stem: Washing soda is a
solution: Washing soda, \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\), is the salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (\(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\)); its aqueous solution is basic, so it is a basic salt. Matches option D.

stem: Baking soda is a mixture of:
optA: Sodium hydrogen carbonate and tartaric acid
optC: Sodium hydrogen carbonate and acetic acid
solution: The intended answer is the composition of baking powder: sodium hydrogen carbonate (\(\text{NaHCO}_3\)) together with a mild edible acid, tartaric acid. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Stem says 'baking soda' but the composition asked for (a mixture of NaHCO3 + tartaric acid) is that of BAKING POWDER; baking soda alone is just NaHCO3. Keyed the intended option A; verify against LWS key.

stem: What do all acids and all bases have in common?
optA: all acids and bases release \(\text{OH}^-\) ions in solution
optB: all acids and bases form ions in solution
optC: all acids release \(\text{OH}^-\) and bases release \(\text{H}^+\) ions in solution
optD: all acids and bases release \(\text{H}^+\) ions in solution
solution: Both acids and bases are electrolytes that ionise in water (acids give \(\text{H}^+\), bases give \(\text{OH}^-\)). The common feature is that both form ions in solution. Matches option B.

stem: A few statements regarding the properties of bases are given below. Mark the correct statements. (1) Sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide are soluble in water. (2) Calcium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide are partially soluble in water. (3) All metallic hydroxides react with acids to form their respective metallic salts. (4) Metallic oxides are acidic oxides, hence they react with acids to form salts.
solution: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong because metallic oxides are BASIC oxides (not acidic); they react with acids to form salts because they are basic. Hence (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Matches option B.

stem: An aqueous solution of sodium chloride is prepared in distilled water. The pH of this solution is:
solution: Sodium chloride is the salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a strong base (NaOH); it does not hydrolyse, so its solution is neutral with pH 7. Matches option B.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: The following pairs of substances are available in the laboratory: (1) Zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid, (2) Zinc and dilute sodium hydroxide solution, (3) Sodium bicarbonate and dilute hydrochloric acid. Which of these can be used to produce a colourless and odourless gas which gives a pop sound on burning?
solution: A gas that pops on burning is hydrogen. Zinc reacts with dilute HCl to give \(\text{H}_2\), and zinc (being amphoteric) also reacts with dilute NaOH to give \(\text{H}_2\). Sodium bicarbonate with HCl gives \(\text{CO}_2\) (no pop). So pairs 1 and 2 work. Matches option A.

stem:
Match column I with column II and mark the correct option from the given codes.

| Column I | Column II |
| --- | --- |
| (a) \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) | (i) Used for disinfecting water |
| (b) \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) | (ii) Used for soda-acid fire extinguishers |
| (c) \(\text{CaOCl}_2\) | (iii) Used for removing permanent hardness of water |
| (d) \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}\) | (iv) Used for making Plaster of Paris decorations |
solution: Washing soda (\(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\)) removes permanent hardness (iii); sodium hydrogen carbonate is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers (ii); bleaching powder (\(\text{CaOCl}_2\)) disinfects water (i); plaster of Paris (\(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) is used for decorations (iv). This gives (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv). Matches option B.
reviewNote: Printed Column I lists BOTH (a) and (b) as Na2CO3; (b) should read NaHCO3 (sodium hydrogen carbonate) for the soda-acid fire-extinguisher match. The intended key is still B. Flawed-print -> kept PRIVATE.

stem: Four solutions, namely glucose, alcohol, hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid, filled in four separate beakers, are connected one by one in an electric circuit with a bulb. The solutions in which the bulb will glow when current is passed are:
solution: A bulb glows only if the solution conducts electricity, i.e. it contains ions. Acids ionise in water and conduct, while glucose and alcohol are non-electrolytes. So only hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid make the bulb glow. Matches option C.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Which of the following substances will not give carbon dioxide on treatment with a dilute acid?
solution: Marble and limestone are \(\text{CaCO}_3\) and baking soda is \(\text{NaHCO}_3\); all react with dilute acid to release \(\text{CO}_2\). Lime is \(\text{CaO}\), an oxide that reacts with acid to give only salt and water (no \(\text{CO}_2\)). Matches option C.

stem: Normal salt is
solution: A normal (neutral) salt is formed from a strong acid and a strong base, so it neither hydrolyses nor changes the pH; its solution is neutral with pH 7. Matches option D.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: What happens when dilute HCl is slowly added to copper oxide in a beaker?
solution: Black copper oxide reacts with HCl: \(\text{CuO} + 2\text{HCl} \to \text{CuCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\). The copper(II) chloride formed gives a blue-green solution. Matches option A.

stem: During the preparation of hydrogen chloride gas on a humid day, the gas is usually passed through a guard tube containing calcium chloride. The role of the calcium chloride is to
optC: absorb \(\text{Cl}^-\) ions from the evolved gas
solution: Calcium chloride is a drying agent; in the guard tube it absorbs water vapour so that dry hydrogen chloride gas is obtained. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following is acidic in nature?
solution: Lime juice contains citric acid and is acidic. Lime water and antacids are basic, and human blood is slightly basic (pH about 7.4). Matches option B.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: A solution reacts with crushed egg-shells to give a gas that turns lime-water milky. The solution contains
solution: Egg-shells are calcium carbonate; the gas that turns lime-water milky is \(\text{CO}_2\), which is released only when an acid reacts with the carbonate. Among the options only HCl is an acid. Matches option D.

stem: For the dilution of concentrated acids, we should add
optC: first water into acid and then more acid
optD: both water to concentrated acid and concentrated acid to water
solution: Dilution is highly exothermic, so acid must always be added slowly to water (with stirring) so the heat is dissipated safely. Adding water to acid can cause dangerous spurting. Matches option A.

stem: Bottle A contains oxalic acid and bottle B contains sodium carbonate solution. When pH paper is dipped in each of the solutions, the colours seen in A and B respectively are
solution: Oxalic acid is acidic (low pH) and turns pH paper orange/red; sodium carbonate is basic (high pH) and turns it blue. So A is orange and B is blue. Matches option A.

stem: The acid produced in the stomach is:
solution: The gastric glands of the stomach secrete hydrochloric acid, \(\text{HCl}\), which aids digestion. Matches option C.

stem: Which one of the following can be used as an acid-base indicator by a visually impaired student?
solution: Vanilla essence is an olfactory indicator: its smell vanishes in a basic solution, so its change can be detected by smell rather than colour. Matches option B.

stem: Name the substance which, on treatment with chlorine, yields bleaching powder.
solution: Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime: \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \to \text{CaOCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\). Matches option B.

stem: Tooth decay begins at the pH of:
solution: Tooth decay sets in when the pH in the mouth falls below about 5.5. Of the given values, only 5.1 is below this threshold, so decay begins at pH 5.1. Matches option B.
reviewNote: NCERT states tooth decay starts when pH falls below 5.5 (not an option). Keyed 5.1 as the only value below the 5.5 threshold; verify against LWS key.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: An acid can react with
solution: Dilute acids react with carbonates to give a salt, water and \(\text{CO}_2\): \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \to 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\). The other three are salts of strong acids and do not react with dilute acid. Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following phenomena occur when a small amount of acid is added to water? (1) Ionization (2) Neutralization (3) Dilution (4) Salt formation
solution: Adding acid to water causes the acid to ionise (release \(\text{H}^+\)) and, because water is added in excess, the acid is diluted. No base is present, so there is no neutralization or salt formation. Hence (i) and (iii). Matches option A.

stem: Which one of the following natural sources contains oxalic acid?
solution: Tomato contains oxalic acid. (Ant and nettle stings contain methanoic/formic acid and tamarind contains tartaric acid.) Matches option B.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating indigestion?
solution: Indigestion caused by excess stomach acid is treated with an antacid, a mild base that neutralises the acid. Matches option A.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Which of the following substances is an antacid?
solution: An antacid is a mild base. \(\text{Mg(OH)}_2\) (milk of magnesia) is basic and neutralises excess stomach acid. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is used for the dissolution of gold?
solution: Gold dissolves in aqua regia, a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and nitric acid. Matches option A.

stem: Which one of the following compounds changes blue litmus to red?
solution: Only an acid turns blue litmus red. Among the options, \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\) (propanoic acid) is a carboxylic acid; the aldehyde, ketone and alcohol are not acidic. Matches option D.

stem: Plaster of Paris hardens by
optA: releasing out a molecule of water
solution: Plaster of Paris sets when it reacts with water and is rehydrated back to gypsum: \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O} + 1\tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: A student adds a teaspoonful of solid sodium bicarbonate to a test tube containing about 3 mL of acetic acid. He observes that the solid sodium bicarbonate
optA: reacts with acetic acid and a clear solution is obtained
optB: floats on the surface of acetic acid
optC: settles down in the test tube
optD: remains suspended in the acetic acid
solution: Sodium bicarbonate reacts with acetic acid with brisk effervescence of \(\text{CO}_2\), forming soluble sodium acetate, so a clear solution is obtained: \(\text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \to \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\). Matches option A.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Acetic acid was added to a solid X kept in a test tube. A colourless, odourless gas Y was evolved. The gas was passed through lime-water, which turned milky. It was concluded that
optA: X is sodium bicarbonate and Y is \(\text{SO}_2\)
optB: X is sodium bicarbonate and Y is \(\text{CO}_2\)
optC: X is sodium acetate and Y is \(\text{CO}_2\)
optD: X is sodium hydroxide and Y is \(\text{CO}_2\)
solution: A gas that turns lime-water milky is \(\text{CO}_2\); it is released when acetic acid reacts with a carbonate/bicarbonate. So X is sodium bicarbonate and Y is \(\text{CO}_2\). Matches option B.

stem: Certain chemical properties of a substance are given below. (1) It turns methyl orange red. (2) It turns turmeric paper red. (3) It reacts with zinc and a gas is evolved. (4) It reacts with solid sodium carbonate to give brisk effervescence. Which of the above properties are shown by dilute sodium hydroxide?
solution: Sodium hydroxide is a base. (1) is wrong (methyl orange turns red in acid, yellow in base) and (4) is an acid property. A base turns turmeric red (2) and reacts with zinc, an amphoteric metal, to release hydrogen (3). So (ii) and (iii) only. Matches option A.

stem: Blue copper sulphate crystals are heated strongly in a dry test tube. Which of the following observations are correct? (1) A white coloured residue is left behind in the test tube. (2) Water droplets are observed on the upper cooler part of the test tube. (3) On adding water to the residue, the colour changes to green.
solution: Heating hydrated copper sulphate (\(\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) drives off its water of crystallization: a white anhydrous residue forms (1) and water vapour condenses on the cooler part (2). On adding water the colour returns to BLUE, not green, so (3) is wrong. Hence I and II only. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Original Q47 references a figure ('Observe the given figure carefully') showing blue copper sulphate crystals heated in a dry test tube; the figure content has been folded into the stem so the item is self-contained.

stem: What happens when two drops of phenolphthalein are added to a dilute solution of NaOH?
solution: NaOH is a base, and phenolphthalein is pink in a basic medium. Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following salts contain water of crystallization? (1) Gypsum (2) Epsom salt (3) Blue vitriol (4) Glauber's salt
solution: All four are hydrated salts: gypsum \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\), Epsom salt \(\text{MgSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}\), blue vitriol \(\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\) and Glauber's salt \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\). Matches option B.

stem: Select washing soda from the following:
solution: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: Which gas is liberated when HCl is added to a sample of solid \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\)?
solution: Acid on a carbonate releases carbon dioxide: \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \to 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\). Matches option A.

stem: Washing soda has the formula
solution: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\). Matches option D.
reviewNote: Internal duplicate of Q50 (washing soda = Na2CO3.10H2O); kept PRIVATE to avoid a public-bank duplicate.

stem: When concentrated acid is added to \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), the reaction is:
solution: Dissolving a concentrated acid in water releases a large amount of heat, so the dilution is exothermic. Matches option A.

stem: Lime water is:
solution: Lime water is a solution of calcium hydroxide, \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\), in water. Matches option B.

stem: A compound is prepared from gypsum upon heating to a temperature of 373 K. Which of the following is incorrect about this compound?
optA: If heated to a higher temperature, the compound becomes dehydrated and is called dead burnt plaster.
optB: When mixed with water and left for half an hour, this compound sets into a liquid mass.
optC: When mixed with water and left for half an hour, this compound sets into a hard mass.
optD: The formula of the compound is calcium sulphate dihydrate.
solution: Heating gypsum to 373 K gives plaster of Paris, \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}\). It sets into a HARD mass with water (so statement b, 'liquid mass', is incorrect). Matches option B.
reviewNote: Two statements are factually incorrect: (b) 'sets into a liquid mass' [it sets into a hard mass] and (d) 'calcium sulphate dihydrate' [PoP is the HEMIhydrate CaSO4.1/2H2O; dihydrate is gypsum]. Keyed (b) as the blatant contradiction with (c); verify against LWS key.

stem: Which of the following gives the correct increasing order of acidic strength?
optA: Hydrochloric acid < Sodium chloride < Acetic acid
optB: Sodium chloride < Acetic acid < Hydrochloric acid
optC: Acetic acid < Sodium chloride < Hydrochloric acid
optD: Sodium chloride < Hydrochloric acid < Acetic acid
solution: Sodium chloride is a neutral salt (least acidic), acetic acid is a weak acid and hydrochloric acid is a strong acid. So the increasing order is Sodium chloride < Acetic acid < Hydrochloric acid. Matches option B.

stem: Soda-lime is a mixture of NaOH and CaO. What is the ratio of NaOH and CaO in soda-lime?
solution: Soda-lime is a mixture of sodium hydroxide and calcium oxide (with the calcium oxide in large excess). The printed numerical options do not correspond to any standard composition ratio.
reviewNote: Options are non-standard decimal values with no derivable chemistry basis; soda-lime has no single fixed NaOH:CaO ratio. Keyed (a) as a placeholder; verify against LWS key (likely a corrupted/auto-generated item).

stem: Bleaching powder is used in the paper industry as a
solution: Bleaching powder releases chlorine, which bleaches; in the paper industry it is used as a bleaching agent for wood pulp. Matches option B.

stem: Which among the following is not a base?
solution: NaOH, KOH and \(\text{NH}_4\text{OH}\) are bases, but \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}\) (ethanol) is a neutral alcohol, not a base. Matches option B.

stem: A scale for measuring the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution is called
solution: The pH scale measures the hydrogen ion (\(\text{H}^+\)) concentration of a solution, from 0 to 14. Matches option B.

stem: The \(\text{H}^+\) ion concentration of a solution is \(1.0 \times 10^{-5}\) M. The solution is
solution: \(\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+] = -\log(10^{-5}) = 5\). A pH of 5 is below 7, so the solution is acidic. Matches option A.

stem: \(\text{NaCl}\) and \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) belong to the family of
solution: \(\text{NaCl}\) is a chloride and \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) is a sulphate, so neither 'chloride salts' nor 'sulphate salts' covers both; the feature common to both is the sodium cation, so both are sodium salts. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Both 'sodium salts' (c) and 'neutral salts' (b) are defensible (both are normal/neutral salts). Keyed (c) as the unambiguous shared family (the common cation); verify against LWS key.

stem: \(\text{HNO}_3\) is a strong acid because:
optA: it does dissociate into ions at all
optB: it does not dissociate into ions at all
optC: it dissociates partially in aqueous solution
optD: it dissociates completely in aqueous solution
solution: A strong acid ionises almost completely in water. \(\text{HNO}_3\) dissociates completely into \(\text{H}^+\) and \(\text{NO}_3^-\). Matches option D.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: A solution reacts with crushed egg shells to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The solution contains
solution: Egg-shells are calcium carbonate; the gas that turns lime-water milky is \(\text{CO}_2\), released only by an acid acting on the carbonate. The only acid among the options is HCl. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Internal duplicate of Q29 (egg-shells -> CO2 -> acid is HCl); kept PRIVATE to avoid a public-bank duplicate.

stem: If the pH of a solution is 13, it means that it is
solution: A pH of 13 is close to the top of the scale (14), so the solution is strongly basic. Matches option B.

stem: Four solutions P, Q, R and S have pH 2, 7, 9 and 13 respectively. Which of the solutions will turn phenolphthalein pink?
solution: Phenolphthalein turns pink only in basic solutions (pH above about 8.3). R (pH 9) and S (pH 13) are basic, so both turn it pink. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following is not a mineral acid?
solution: Nitric, sulphuric and hydrochloric acids are mineral (inorganic) acids; citric acid is an organic acid found in fruits. Matches option D.

stem: The oxide which can react with HCl as well as KOH to give the corresponding salt and water is
solution: An oxide that reacts with both an acid and a base is amphoteric. \(\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\) is amphoteric (the others are basic oxides), so it reacts with both HCl and KOH. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following gives \(\text{CO}_2\) on heating?
solution: Limestone (\(\text{CaCO}_3\)) decomposes on heating: \(\text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2\). Quick lime (\(\text{CaO}\)) and slaked lime (\(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\)) give no \(\text{CO}_2\), and soda ash is stable to ordinary heating. Matches option B.

stem: As the pH value of a solution increases from 7 to 14, it represents
optA: a decrease in the concentration of \(\text{OH}^-\) ions
optB: an increase in the concentration of \(\text{OH}^-\) ions
optC: no change in the concentration of \(\text{OH}^-\) ions
optD: an increase in the concentration of \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^+\) ions
solution: Higher pH means a more basic solution, i.e. a greater concentration of hydroxide ions (and fewer \(\text{H}^+\) ions). So as pH rises from 7 to 14 the \(\text{OH}^-\) concentration increases. Matches option B.

stem: The name of the salt used to remove permanent hardness of water is:
solution: Washing soda, sodium carbonate decahydrate, removes permanent hardness by precipitating the \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) and \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) ions as insoluble carbonates. Matches option B.

stem: When bleaching powder is treated with \(\text{CO}_2\):
solution: \(\text{CaOCl}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \to \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{Cl}_2\); carbon dioxide displaces chlorine from bleaching powder, forming calcium carbonate and chlorine. Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following turns red litmus blue?
solution: An aqueous solution of ammonia is basic (\(\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{NH}_4\text{OH}\)) and turns red litmus blue. Dry gases do not affect litmus, and HCl is acidic. Matches option B.

stem: HCl is a strong acid since in solution it gives
solution: Acidic strength depends on the number of hydrogen ions released. HCl ionises almost completely, giving a large number of \(\text{H}^+\) ions, so it is a strong acid. Matches option D.

subtopic: Neutralization and Reactions of Acids and Bases
stem: When HCl reacts with granulated zinc
optA: the odour of chlorine is observed
optB: the surface of the metal turns shining
optD: a colourless and odourless gas evolves with bubbles
solution: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid to give zinc chloride and hydrogen: \(\text{Zn} + 2\text{HCl} \to \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\). Hydrogen is a colourless, odourless gas seen as bubbles. Matches option D.
